title: Migrating to 1.4 breaks pickeling of joinloaded relationships
body:
### Describe the bug

Pickeling an object loaded with `session.query(Child).options(joinedload(Child.parent), raiseload("*").first()` fails if `Parent` has relationship(s) of it's own because the `PathToken` object created in that case fails to be pickled. The issue occurred after migrating from 1.3 to 1.4 (independent of the `future`-flag). 

### To Reproduce

```python
from pickle import dumps

import sqlalchemy as sa
from sqlalchemy import orm, schema

print("SQLAlchemy", sa.__version__)

metadata = schema.MetaData()


@orm.as_declarative(metadata=metadata)
class Base:

    @orm.declared_attr
    def __tablename__(cls):
        return cls.__name__.lower()



class Grandparent(Base):

    id = sa.Column(sa.Integer, primary_key=True)


class Parent(Base):

    id = sa.Column(sa.Integer, primary_key=True)
    grandparent_id = sa.Column(sa.ForeignKey("grandparent.id", ondelete="CASCADE"), nullable=False)
    grandparent = orm.relationship(Grandparent)


class Child(Base):

    id = sa.Column(sa.Integer, primary_key=True)
    parent_id = sa.Column(sa.ForeignKey("parent.id", ondelete="CASCADE"), nullable=False)
    parent = orm.relationship(Parent)


def set_up_example_data(engine):
    metadata.create_all(engine)
    with orm.Session(engine) as session:
        grandparent = Grandparent()
        session.add(grandparent)
        parent = Parent(grandparent=grandparent)
        session.add(parent)
        session.add(Child(parent=parent))
        session.commit()


def main():
    engine = sa.create_engine("sqlite+pysqlite:///:memory:", future=True)
    set_up_example_data(engine)

    with orm.Session(engine) as session:
        child = session.query(Child).options(
            orm.joinedload(Child.parent),
            orm.raiseload("*"),
        ).first()

    # This raises an AttributeError:
    dumps(child)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```


### Error

```
SQLAlchemy 1.4.25
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "./it_is_a_pickle.py", line 65, in <module>
    main()
  File "./it_is_a_pickle.py", line 61, in main
    dumps(child)
  File "/home/milan/Code/sqlalchemy_pickle/env/lib/python3.8/site-packages/sqlalchemy/orm/strategy_options.py", line 631, in __getstate__
    d["path"] = self.path.serialize()
  File "/home/milan/Code/sqlalchemy_pickle/env/lib/python3.8/site-packages/sqlalchemy/orm/path_registry.py", line 178, in serialize
    return self._serialize_path(path)
  File "/home/milan/Code/sqlalchemy_pickle/env/lib/python3.8/site-packages/sqlalchemy/orm/path_registry.py", line 134, in _serialize_path
    [m.class_ for m in [path[i] for i in range(0, len(path), 2)]],
  File "/home/milan/Code/sqlalchemy_pickle/env/lib/python3.8/site-packages/sqlalchemy/orm/path_registry.py", line 134, in <listcomp>
    [m.class_ for m in [path[i] for i in range(0, len(path), 2)]],
AttributeError: 'PathToken' object has no attribute 'class_'
```

### Versions

- OS: Ubuntu 20.04.3
- Python: 3.8.10 (also tested with 3.7 on Debian with the same result)
- SQLAlchemy: 1.4.25 (also tested with 1.4.0 with the same result)
